what: emberdays: counting the days hot enough to feed a fire
title: emberdays: counting the days hot enough to feed a fire
text: Counting days hot enough feed fire. Documentation website: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-gauravwarke/ emberdays helps people living bushfire-prone parts Australia answer one question: city, hot days bushfire season common now early 1900s? Hot days dry bush drive dangerous fire weather. study 2019–20 fires found rising temperature main reason fire weather got worse southeastern Australia (van Oldenborgh et al., 2021). package gives : Data: fire_season_temps, daily maximum temperatures fire-season months (September February) one Bureau Meteorology station seven cities, 1910 February 2019. stations describes station. Functions question: count_hot_days() counts days temperature threshold fire season flags seasons missing data. compare_periods() sets early period recent one. describe_change() turns comparison one plain-English sentence. Functions data: count_exceedances() works daily series, whatever column names. counts days threshold calendar year, July–June year season define. season_year() labels seasons. See -data guide. app: launch_app() opens Shiny app choose city, “hot day” threshold, part season two periods compare.

title: Compare hot days in an early period with a recent period — compare_periods
text: hot_days tibble returned count_hot_days() count_exceedances(). early Two years giving first last season early period. code: count_exceedances(   data,   value,   threshold,   direction = c("above", "below"),   date = "date",   start_month = 1,   months = 1:12,   min_coverage = 0.9 )

title: Count days above (or below) a threshold in each season-year — count_exceedances
text: data data frame one row per day single place. Filter one place calling (see examples). value name column holding daily value, quotes, example "max_temp". threshold value compare day . direction "" counts days threshold; "" counts days . date name column holding dates (class Date), quotes. Defaults "date". start_month month season-year starts (1 12). Defaults 1, ordinary calendar year. Use 9 southern fire season, 7 July-June year. months months include. Defaults 12. example, c(12, 1, 2) keeps summer. min_coverage share days season must value season marked complete. Defaults 0.9.

text: tibble one row per season-year columns season_start, season (label "2018-19", "2018" calendar years), days_possible, days_recorded, coverage, n_exceed (days meeting threshold), extreme (highest value "", lowest "") complete.

title: Describe a change between two periods in plain English — describe_change
text: Turns two-row table compare_periods() one sentence non-specialist can read, "Perth, days 35 degrees C become common: ...". sentence states direction, averages, size change , meaningful, ratio. also says period usable seasons, instead reporting misleading number.

title: Describe a change between two periods in plain English — describe_change
text: comparison tibble returned compare_periods(). plural noun phrase counted, example "days 35 degrees C" "frosty nights". place Optional place name start sentence . tolerance Differences smaller (days per season) described "". Defaults 0.5. digits Decimal places averages. Defaults 1.

title: Describe a change between two periods in plain English — describe_change
text: single character string.

title: Describe a change between two periods in plain English — describe_change
code: perth <- count_hot_days(fire_season_temps, "Perth") compare_periods(perth) |>   describe_change(what = "days at or above 35 degrees C", place = "Perth") #> [1] "In Perth, days at or above 35 degrees C have become more common: recent seasons (1989–2018) averaged 26.0 per season, compared with 17.0 in 1910–1939, an increase of 9.0 per season (1.5 times the early average)."  # When a period has no data, the sentence says so count_hot_days(fire_season_temps, "Brisbane") |>   compare_periods() |>   describe_change(what = "very hot days", place = "Brisbane") #> [1] "In Brisbane, the early period (1910–1939) has no complete seasons, so no change can be stated."
